correctness.rationale: The exact factorization follows from exhaustive selected/absent local domination cases. \(U_t\) factors are positive and log-concave, so \(P=(1+x)U_aU_c\) is log-concave. \(Q=P-x^{a+c}\) loses only one coefficient. The only endangered Turán inequality has exactly derived polynomial margin \(144(q_s^2-q_{s-1}q_{s+1})\), bounded strictly below by a positive explicit expression via \(4ac\le(a+c)^2\). Q and all \(U_t\) are hole-free, and convolution preserves log-concavity. The actual code checks 192 complete enumerations, 18,045 independent 3-state tree-DP cases, and 6,400 exact margin cases; these supplement, not replace, the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Du–Heilman–Panova (2026), Theorem 3.3 and Remark 3.4, prove only the strictly positive pendant-multiplicity case and explicitly leave zero groups open. The corrected local factor and uniform log-concavity inequality for one missing group are not derived there. Şahin–Şahin (2018) enumerate certain caterpillar domination polynomials but do not prove the present log-concavity extension. Wang (2026) covers short-legged spiders, not arbitrary multi-support caterpillars; Beaton–Schoonhoven (2024) cover unimodality under another hypothesis. Targeted mathematical-record and literature searches found no encompassing statement. Priority remains qualified by incomplete global indexing.
residual_risks: Global historical-priority coverage is not a proof of novelty; an alternative terminology or unindexed earlier log-concavity result could exist.
The nearly well-dominated tree paper was not used for full-text negative claims; its abstract gives only a weaker result under extra hypotheses.
The theorem assumes exactly one bare interior spine vertex; it does not settle the stronger conjecture with two or more missing groups.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper explicitly proposes extending domination-coefficient log-concavity from fully leaf-supported caterpillars to missing-leaf spine vertices. The theorem settles the natural exact-one-missing-group case for all spine lengths and arbitrary positive pendant multiplicities, not a finite census or a textbook substitution. Its new structural factorization reduces all potential coefficient failures to one nontrivial two-parameter inequality, proved uniformly by a degree-six positivity bound, supplying a potential local module for analyzing multiple gaps.
